Jute fibers are derived from the highly lignified sclerenchyma cells in the phloem tissue of mature stems that grow to a height of 2 to 4 m.
The plant thrives in rich, loamy alluvial soils that are well watered.
Generally, it takes about 100 to 120 days for jute to mature before harvest usually in June in lowland areas in India
During harvest, plants are cut close to the ground and then sorted according to stem thickness.
Cut and sorted stems are stacked to dry in the field and tied into bundles.
After 3 days, the dried stems are defoliated by hand and then transported to an area with flowing water.

There are two broad groups of bamboo, thickbamboo and thin reed like bamboo (ringal).
Bamboo is a thick, long and slender like plant (Figure 1) while ringal is thin spineless plant
Ringal species grow at mid and high hill areas of the state (> 2000 m) while bamboo is generally found at mid and low hills (<2000 m).
Among ringal species, dev-ringal (H. falconeri) is the most commonly used species for making different articles.
Himalayacalamus falconeri is recorded at highest elevations among all the bamboo species.
